test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Chetan travels from City A to City B. If Chetan drives his car at 2/3 of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 46 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Chetan would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **distance** is **constant**, **speed** is inversely proportional to **time**.

Ratio of **Speed** = 3 : 2 → Ratio of **Time** = 2 : 3

Difference in time units = 3 − 2 = 1 unit

Given, 1 unit = 46 minutes

Normal time = 2 units = 2 × 46 = 92 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 92 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2a02f9417088cc2238f951730fc608a5d757ad451e900d06181c39be1302991.png] 

**Given:** Reduced speed = 2/3 of normal speed. Delay = 46 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Let **Normal Speed** = S and **Normal Time** = T.

⇒ Distance = S × T

⇒ New Speed = (2/3)S and New Time = T + 46

⇒ Distance = (2/3)S × (T + 46)

⇒ S × T = (2/3)S × (T + 46)

⇒ T = 2/3 (T + 46)

⇒ 3T = 2T + 92

⇒ T = 92 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 92 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

For a constant distance, speed and time are inversely proportional (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

General Formula for Late/Early Time

If a person travels at a/b of their usual speed, the usual time taken is [Late time × a / (b − a)].

Average Speed

When distances are equal, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ + S₂).</p
